study: panel-method (vortex lattice / lifting surface) KP505 open-water sweep on the anchor J grid, with a panel-density and wake-model study
configuration_rationale: n_radial=16 / n_chord=2 sits in the well-conditioned band of the lattice (condition number < 1e3; finer radial meshes without the strip-width core regularisation pick up the odd-even mode, see docs/m7485_kp505_openwater_bem.md §5); the geometric wake is the only model of the three that stays physical down to J = 0.1 (kinematic and induced helices collapse as tan(beta_w) = J/(2 pi r) -> 0).

design_advance_ratio.derivation: argmax over the transcribed anchor table of eta_0 = J K_T / (2 pi K_Q); derived in code, not recalled
design_advance_ratio.secondary_note: J = 0.7 is reported as well because it is the usual nominal design point quoted for this propeller class; no threshold is attached to it

criteria.statement: |d eta_0| <= 5.0% at every anchor advance ratio (10 points)
all anchor points reported (no selection of passing points) and the deviation signs share one physical explanation

verdict.gap_statement: C1 asks |dK_T| <= 3.0% at J = 0.8 and measured -29.13%; C2 asks |d eta_0| <= 5.0% at all 10 points and the worst is 786.67% at J = 1.0 (the |d eta_0| <= 5.0% band is met at 1 of 10 points). The Richardson-extrapolated lattice values (K_T = {'0.4': 0.3141321821632644, '0.7': 0.1492704506833062, '0.9': 0.027500459224397884}) do not close the gap either, and the radial-ladder GCI on K_T is 7.1-8.1% at J = (0.4, 0.7, 0.9), i.e. the *discretisation* of this lattice is itself larger than the 3% design-point band. What is left is a geometry/model gap: the published particulars fix only six scalars, so the chord and radial pitch distributions and the NACA66 camber are reconstructed or absent and the sections are flat. The lattice breaks down near zero loading: K_T < 0 at J = [1.0] and the momentum gate fails there, so those points are reported as unphysical rather than dropped.
